title: Arbitrary-Order Block SignSGD for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
claim: Our method converges fastest per token and per wall-clock time against baselines, and its distributed variant scales robustly with agent count.
layout: 3 line-plot panels in a row, shared y-axis, legends inside each plot
description: Three side-by-side line plots with training loss on the y-axis, from 0.20 to 0.50. The left plot has tokens on the x-axis and compares LoRA, Galore, BAdam, Apollo, ABSignSGD-MV and ABSignSGD. The red ABSignSGD curve, with ABSignSGD-MV overlapping it, drops fastest and ends lowest at about 0.24. The baselines level off higher, between about 0.26 and 0.29. The middle plot uses wall-clock time in seconds on the x-axis. The red ABSignSGD curve ends early at a low loss, and slower baselines run much longer. The right plot shows loss against iterations for ABSignSGD at batch sizes 16 to 128 and for ABSignSGD-MV, drawn in cyan. All curves overlap closely, which shows the MV variant scales with agent count. Legends sit inside each panel, and gridlines are light.
caption: Training loss for Qwen3-8B on OpenMathInstruct-2. Left & Middle: Convergence comparison against baselines in terms of tokens and wall-clock time (ABSignSGD-MV is excluded for time comparison as it uses multiple agents). ABSignSGD achieves the fastest reduction in both metrics. Right: Robustness of ABSignSGD-MV. The curves show loss vs. iterations as the number of agents increases from 1 to 32 (fixing local batch size). The MV variant closely tracks the singleagent baseline regardless of the agent count, demonstrating high scalability.
abstract: We propose \textbf{ABSignSGD}, a block‑coordinate variant of sign-based descent with flexible block selection that enables memory‑ and runtime‑efficient full‑parameter fine‑tuning of large language models. We present a unified convergence analysis under mild conditions, covering both the base method and a \textit{majority‑vote} extension for distributed training. The latter improves communication efficiency by aggregating only gradient signs rather than averaging full gradients. Experiments on \textcolor{blue}{Qwen3‑8B, Llama3-8B, and Qwen3-32B}, spanning mathematical reasoning and general instruction‑following tasks, show that ABSignSGD converges faster per iteration and delivers superior downstream performance while reducing both runtime and memory usage compared to existing methods. Ablation studies further indicate that the memoryless sign-based update naturally complements block‑wise updates, explaining the method’s strong empirical performance.
